-- ── durable variable storage ──────────────────────────────────────────── -- MUSHclient keeps SetVariable data in the world's plugin-state file. That -- file is per world, and it is lost when a plugin is reinstalled by hand -- instead of reloaded - which is why settings here kept resetting. These -- wrappers keep the same SetVariable/GetVariable API but also write to -- PortalValue.dat next to the plugin, so the data survives both. -- GetPluginInfo(id, 6) is the plugin FILE path, not its folder, so the -- filename has to be stripped off. do local realGet, realSet = GetVariable, SetVariable local dir = (GetPluginInfo (GetPluginID (), 6) or ""):match ("^(.*[\\/])") or "" local path = dir .. "PortalValue.dat" local store = {}
local function flush () local out = io.open (path, "w") if not out then return end local keys = {} for k in pairs (store) do keys[#keys + 1] = k end table.sort (keys) out:write ("-- PortalValue saved variables. Written by the plugin.\n") out:write ("return {\n") for _, k in ipairs (keys) do out:write (string.format (" [%q] = %q,\n", k, store[k])) end out:write ("}\n") out:close () end
local fh = io.open (path, "r") if fh then local body = fh:read ("*a") fh:close () local chunk = loadstring (body or "") if chunk then local ok, t = pcall (chunk) if ok and type (t) == "table" then store = t end end else -- first run: take a copy of whatever the old plugin-variable storage -- still holds, and write it out at once so it can't be lost later local ok, list = pcall (GetVariableList) if ok and type (list) == "table" then for k, v in pairs (list) do store[tostring (k)] = tostring (v) end end flush () end
function SetVariable (name, value) name, value = tostring (name), tostring (value) if store[name] ~= value then store[name] = value flush () end return realSet (name, value) -- keep the old storage in step as well end
function GetVariable (name) local v = store[tostring (name)] if v ~= nil then return v end return realGet (name) -- falls back while migrating end
function DeleteVariable (name) store[tostring (name)] = nil flush () return realSet (name, "") end end -- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
require "serialize"
local MAPPER_ID = "b6eae87ccedd84f510b74714" local GMCP_ID = "3e7dedbe37e44942dd46d264"
-- theme colours local VERSION = "5.0" -- keep in step with the version= attribute above
local C = { hdr="@x099", val="@x045", num="@W", ok="@x048", bad="@R" }
-- colour output (fall back to plain text if the colour lib isn't available) local have_colors = pcall(require, "aardwolf_colors") function pv_echo(s) if have_colors then AnsiNote(ColoursToANSI(s)) else Note((s:gsub("@x%d%d?%d?", ""):gsub("@%a", ""))) end end local echo = pv_echo -- PortalDex code calls echo()
local function esc(s) return (tostring(s or ""):gsub("@", "@@")) end
-- Landing-room tag for a catalogued portal: " (33994)" when the mapper has -- exactly one saved destination for that item, " (7 dests)" when it has many -- (plain chaos portals), and "" until the mapper has been cross-referenced. local function pd_room_tag(e) if e.room then return " "..C.ok.."("..tostring(e.room)..")" end if e.rooms_n and e.rooms_n > 1 then return " "..C.ok.."("..e.rooms_n.." dests)" end return "" end local function q(s) return "'" .. tostring(s):gsub("'", "''") .. "'" end
-- locate the mapper's sqlite db (adapts to whatever world/char/install we're in) local function get_db_path() if not IsPluginInstalled(MAPPER_ID) then return nil, "the Aardwolf GMCP mapper plugin is not installed" end local db_name = GetPluginVariable(MAPPER_ID, "db_name") if not db_name or db_name == "" then db_name = (WorldName() or ""):gsub("[^%w%s()_-]", ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") end if db_name == "" then return nil, "could not determine the mapper's database name" end local path = GetInfo(66) .. db_name .. ".db" local f = io.open(path, "rb") if not f then return nil, "database file not found at: " .. path end f:close() return path end
local CARDINALS = { n=true, s=true, e=true, w=true, u=true, d=true }
-- turn an ordered list of step commands into a compressed speedwalk + a move count local function build_speedwalk(dirs) local segs, run = {}, {} local moves = 0 local function flush() if #run > 0 then local parts = {} for _, rc in ipairs(run) do parts[#parts+1] = ((rc.c > 1) and rc.c or "") .. rc.d end segs[#segs+1] = "run " .. table.concat(parts) run = {} end end for _, d in ipairs(dirs) do moves = moves + 1 if CARDINALS[d] then local last = run[#run] if last and last.d == d then last.c = last.c + 1 else run[#run+1] = { d = d, c = 1 } end else flush() segs[#segs+1] = d end end flush() return table.concat(segs, ";"), moves end
local function recall_line(rooms, sw, msg) if rooms ~= nil then if rooms == 0 then return C.hdr .. "Recall walk : " .. C.val .. "you're standing on recall" end return C.hdr .. "Recall walk : " .. C.num .. rooms .. C.hdr .. " rooms (no portals) " .. C.ok .. (sw ~= "" and esc(sw) or "") end return C.hdr .. "Recall walk : " .. C.hdr .. "(" .. esc(msg or "unknown") .. ")" end
-- ========================================================================= -- =============== CATALOG (formerly the PortalDex plugin) =============== -- =========================================================================
-- catalog[idnumber] = { id, name, kw, ptype, restrung, leads, found, level, t, refs } catalog = catalog or {} pd_bag = pd_bag or "" -- portal container keyword pd_cmd = pd_cmd or "" -- custom portal command (besides take/get) if pd_auto == nil then pd_auto = true end -- catalog-as-you-go on/off scan_active = false -- a scan is running? scan_queue = scan_queue or {} pd_speed = pd_speed or 2.0 -- seconds between scan steps scan_mode = nil -- "missing" => auto-repeat scan_pass_start = 0 scan_rechecked = {} -- stale golden ids re-id'd this scan pd_scan_current_ref = "" -- ref being scanned right now
-- ---- catalog persistence: own file (survives reinstalls) ---- local function pd_datafile() return GetInfo(66) .. "PortalDex_data.lua" end
local function pd_save() local path = pd_datafile() local tmp = path .. ".tmp" local f = io.open(tmp, "w") if not f then return end f:write("return " .. serialize.save_simple({ catalog = catalog, bag = pd_bag, cmd = pd_cmd, auto = pd_auto, speed = pd_speed })) f:close() os.remove(path) os.rename(tmp, path) end
local function pd_read_table(path) local f = io.open(path, "r") if not f then return nil end local content = f:read("*a"); f:close() if not content or content == "" then return nil end local ok, data = pcall(function() return assert(loadstring(content))() end) if ok and type(data) == "table" then return data end return nil end
local function pd_load() local data = pd_read_table(pd_datafile()) or pd_read_table(pd_datafile() .. ".tmp") if data then if type(data.catalog) == "table" then catalog = data.catalog end pd_bag = data.bag or pd_bag pd_cmd = data.cmd or pd_cmd if data.auto ~= nil then pd_auto = data.auto end if tonumber(data.speed) then pd_speed = tonumber(data.speed) end end end
-- ---- id-box capture ---- -- We anchor on the "Keywords" line (always the first row of an Aardwolf id box) -- rather than toggling on "+----+" borders. Aardwolf prints borders all over the -- place (other id's, score, tables); an odd stray one used to desync the old -- toggle and silently drop the capture. This is immune to that. local collecting = false local buf = {}
function pd_border() -- a border while we're collecting a real record = the box just closed if collecting and #buf > 0 then pd_parse(buf); collecting = false; buf = {} end end
function pd_line(name, line, wc) local content = wc[1] if content:match("^%s*Keywords%s*:") then if collecting and #buf > 0 then pd_parse(buf) end -- flush a prior unclosed box buf = { content }; collecting = true return end if collecting then buf[#buf+1] = content end end
local function classify(kw, flagset, found) kw = (kw or ""):lower() found = (found or ""):lower() local chaos = (flagset["nosac"] and flagset["nosteal"]) or kw:find("chaos portal", 1, true) if chaos then if flagset["precious"] or kw:find("golden", 1, true) then return "golden chaos" end return "chaos" end if kw:find("trivia", 1, true) then return "trivia" end if found == "a bad trip" then return "trivia" end return "gameload" end
function pd_parse(lines) local f, cur = {}, nil for _, raw in ipairs(lines) do local label = raw:match("^%s*([%a][%a%s']-)%s*:") if label and not raw:match("^%s*:") then local val = raw:match(":%s*(.-)%s*$") or "" label = label:gsub("%s+$",""):gsub("%s+"," ") f[label] = val cur = label else local cont = raw:match("^%s*:%s*(.-)%s*$") if cont and cur then f[cur] = (f[cur] or "") .. ", " .. cont end end end
if not (f["Id"] and f["Type"]) then return end if not f["Type"]:match("[Pp]ortal") then return end if not pd_auto and not scan_active then return end
local id = (f["Id"] or ""):match("%d+") if not id then return end
local flagset = {} for w in (f["Flags"] or ""):gmatch("[%w%-]+") do flagset[w:lower()] = true end
local level = (f["Type"] or ""):match("Level%s*:%s*(%d+)") or "?" local kw = f["Keywords"] or "" local existing = catalog[id] local rec = { id = id, name = f["Name"] or "?", kw = kw, ptype = classify(kw, flagset, f["Found at"]), restrung = flagset["restrung"] and true or false, leads = f["Leads to"] or "?", found = f["Found at"] or "?", level = level, t = os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), refs = (existing and existing.refs) or {}, room = existing and existing.room, roomname = existing and existing.roomname, rooms_n = existing and existing.rooms_n, } if scan_active and pd_scan_current_ref ~= "" then rec.refs[pd_scan_current_ref] = true end
local isnew = (existing == nil) catalog[id] = rec pd_save()
if isnew then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] +"..C.ok..esc(rec.ptype)..C.hdr..(rec.restrung and " "..C.val.."(restrung)" or "") .." "..C.val..esc(rec.name).." "..C.num.."("..id..")"..C.hdr.." -> "..C.val..esc(rec.leads)..pd_room_tag(rec)) end end
local pd_stamp_rooms -- forward decl; defined once cross_reference() exists
local function count_types() local counts, total, restrung = {}, 0, 0 for _, r in pairs(catalog) do counts[r.ptype] = (counts[r.ptype] or 0) + 1 total = total + 1 if r.restrung then restrung = restrung + 1 end end return counts, total, restrung end
function pd_summary() local counts, total, restrung = count_types() echo(C.hdr.."============= "..C.num.."PortalDex"..C.hdr.." =============") if total == 0 then echo(C.val.."No portals cataloged yet. 'id' a portal (or run "..C.ok.."portaldex scan"..C.val..").") return end for _, ty in ipairs({"golden chaos","chaos","trivia","gameload"}) do if counts[ty] then echo(C.hdr.." "..C.ok..string.format("%-14s", ty)..C.num..counts[ty]); counts[ty] = nil end end for ty, n in pairs(counts) do echo(C.hdr.." "..C.ok..string.format("%-14s", ty)..C.num..n) end echo(C.hdr.." "..C.val..string.format("%-14s","(restrung)")..C.num..restrung) echo(C.hdr.." "..C.val..string.format("%-14s","total")..C.num..total) echo(C.hdr.."Use "..C.ok.."portaldex list"..C.hdr.." to see them all.") end
function pd_list(name, line, wc) local filter = wc and wc[1] and wc[1]:lower() or nil -- fill in landing rooms for anything catalogued since the last cross-reference local need = false for _, r in pairs(catalog) do if r.rooms_n == nil then need = true; break end end if need then pd_stamp_rooms(true) end local arr = {} for _, r in pairs(catalog) do arr[#arr+1] = r end table.sort(arr, function(a,b) if a.ptype ~= b.ptype then return a.ptype < b.ptype end return (a.name or "") < (b.name or "") end) local shown = 0 echo(C.hdr.."============= "..C.num.."PortalDex list"..C.hdr.." =============") for _, r in ipairs(arr) do local hay = (r.ptype.." "..r.name.." "..r.leads.." "..tostring(r.room or "")):lower() if (not filter) or hay:find(filter, 1, true) then echo(C.ok..string.format("%-13s", r.ptype)..(r.restrung and C.bad.."R " or " ") ..C.val..esc(r.name).." "..C.num.."("..r.id..")"..C.hdr.." -> "..C.val..esc(r.leads)..pd_room_tag(r) ..C.hdr.." lvl "..C.num..esc(r.level)) shown = shown + 1 end end echo(C.hdr.."("..C.num..shown..C.hdr.." shown"..(filter and (", filter '"..esc(wc[1]).."'") or "")..")") end
function pd_clear() catalog = {} pd_save() echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Catalog cleared.") end
-- remove one portal from the catalog, by item id (exact) or by name text (one match) function pd_remove(name, line, wc) local arg = ((wc and wc[1]) or ""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") if arg == "" then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Usage: "..C.ok.."portaldex remove <item id | name>"..C.hdr..". (ids show in "..C.ok.."portaldex list"..C.hdr..".)") return end if arg:match("^%d+$") and catalog[arg] then local nm = catalog[arg].name or "?" catalog[arg] = nil pd_save() echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Removed "..C.val..esc(nm).." "..C.num.."("..arg..")"..C.hdr.." from the catalog.") return end local low = arg:lower() local matches = {} for id, e in pairs(catalog) do local hay = ((e.name or "").." "..(e.ptype or "").." "..(e.leads or "")):lower() if hay:find(low, 1, true) then matches[#matches+1] = { id = id, e = e } end end if #matches == 0 then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] No cataloged portal matches "..C.val.."'"..esc(arg).."'"..C.hdr..".") elseif #matches == 1 then local m = matches[1] catalog[m.id] = nil pd_save() echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Removed "..C.val..esc(m.e.name or "?").." "..C.num.."("..m.id..")"..C.hdr.." from the catalog.") else echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] "..C.num..#matches..C.hdr.." matches — remove by id with "..C.ok.."portaldex remove <id>"..C.hdr..":") for _, m in ipairs(matches) do echo(" "..C.val..esc(m.e.name or "?").." "..C.num.."("..m.id..")"..C.hdr.." ["..C.ok..esc(m.e.ptype or "?")..C.hdr.."]") end end end
function pd_speed_cmd(name, line, wc) local n = tonumber(wc and wc[1]) if not n then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Scan speed: "..C.num..pd_speed..C.hdr.."s per portal. Set with "..C.ok.."portaldex speed <seconds>"..C.hdr..".") return end if n < 0.5 then n = 0.5 elseif n > 10 then n = 10 end pd_speed = n; pd_save() echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Scan speed set to "..C.num..pd_speed..C.hdr.."s per portal.") end
function pd_auto_cmd(name, line, wc) local arg = ((wc and wc[1]) or ""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$",""):lower() if arg == "on" then pd_auto = true elseif arg == "off" then pd_auto = false elseif arg == "" then pd_auto = not pd_auto else echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Use "..C.ok.."portaldex auto on|off"..C.hdr..".") return end pd_save() echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Catalog-as-you-go is "..(pd_auto and (C.ok.."ON") or (C.bad.."OFF")) ..C.hdr..(pd_auto and "." or " — manual id's won't be saved (scans still catalog).")) end
function pd_bag_cmd(name, line, wc) local arg = (wc and wc[1] or ""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") if arg == "" then if pd_bag == "" then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] No portal container set; scans use each command's own container.") else echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Portal container keyword: "..C.val..esc(pd_bag)) end echo(C.hdr.."Set with "..C.ok.."portaldex bag <keyword>"..C.hdr..", clear with "..C.ok.."portaldex bag none"..C.hdr..".") return end if arg:lower() == "none" or arg:lower() == "clear" then pd_bag = ""; pd_save() echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Portal container cleared; scans will use each command's container.") return end pd_bag = arg; pd_save() echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Portal container set to "..C.val..esc(pd_bag)..C.hdr..". Scans will take/put using this bag.") end
-- Custom portal command: an extra verb (besides take/get) that scans look for in -- the mapper's saved portal exits, in the form <verb> <item> [container]. function pd_cmd_cmd(name, line, wc) local arg = (wc and wc[1] or ""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") if arg == "" then if pd_cmd == "" then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] No custom portal command set; scans look for "..C.val.."take"..C.hdr.."/"..C.val.."get"..C.hdr.." only.") else echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Custom portal command: "..C.val..esc(pd_cmd)..C.hdr.." (scans look for it as well as take/get).") end echo(C.hdr.."Set with "..C.ok.."portaldex cmd <word>"..C.hdr..", clear with "..C.ok.."portaldex cmd none"..C.hdr..".") return end if arg:lower() == "none" or arg:lower() == "clear" then pd_cmd = ""; pd_save() echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Custom portal command cleared; scans look for take/get only.") return end pd_cmd = arg; pd_save() echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Custom portal command set to "..C.val..esc(pd_cmd)..C.hdr..". Scans now look for " ..C.val..esc(pd_cmd)..C.hdr.." <item> [container] as well as take/get.") end
-- Pull the item reference (and container) from a portal command: the LAST visible -- id number or keyword used in a take/get/custom command (dungeon portals take a first-room portal, -- nod, then take the real one). Normal portals have one take, so last == only. local function extract_ref(cmd) cmd = cmd or "" -- verbs to look for: take, get, plus the custom command if one is set. -- Each verb becomes a case-insensitive Lua pattern (punctuation escaped). local verbs = { "take", "get" } if pd_cmd and pd_cmd ~= "" then verbs[#verbs+1] = pd_cmd end local pats = {} for _, v in ipairs(verbs) do local p = v:gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") p = p:gsub("[^%w%s]", "%%%0") p = p:gsub("%a", function(c) return "["..c:lower()..c:upper().."]" end) p = p:gsub("%s+", "%%s+") pats[#pats+1] = p end local lastref, lastcont for seg in (cmd .. ";"):gmatch("([^;]*);") do local ref, cont for _, p in ipairs(pats) do ref, cont = seg:match("^%s*"..p.."%s+([^%s;]+)%s+([^%s;]+)") if not ref then ref = seg:match("^%s*"..p.."%s+([^%s;]+)") end if ref then break end end if ref then lastref, lastcont = ref, cont end end return lastref, lastcont end
local function tcount(t) local n=0 for _ in pairs(t) do n=n+1 end return n end
local function build_ref_index() local idx = {} for id, e in pairs(catalog) do if e.refs then for r in pairs(e.refs) do idx[r] = id end end end return idx end
local function resolve_ref(ref, idx) ref = (ref or ""):lower() if ref == "" then return nil end if idx[ref] then return idx[ref] end if ref:match("^%d+$") and catalog[ref] then return ref end for id, e in pairs(catalog) do for w in (e.kw or ""):gmatch("%S+") do w = w:lower() if w == ref or (#ref < #w and w:sub(1, #ref) == ref) then return id end end end return nil end
local function make_cataloged_checker() local idx = build_ref_index() return function(ref) return resolve_ref(ref, idx) ~= nil end end
local function cross_reference() local path, why = get_db_path() if not path then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] "..esc(why or "no mapper db")..".") return nil end local ok_sql, sqlite3 = pcall(require, "sqlite3") if not ok_sql then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] sqlite3 library unavailable.") return nil end local db = sqlite3.open(path) if not db then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] could not open the mapper database.") return nil end local idx = build_ref_index() local byItem, missing, total, noitem = {}, {}, 0, 0 for row in db:nrows([[ SELECT e.dir AS cmd, e.touid AS t, r.name AS nm, r.area AS ar FROM exits e LEFT JOIN rooms r ON r.uid = e.touid WHERE e.fromuid IN ('*','**') ]]) do total = total + 1 local ref = extract_ref(row.cmd) if not ref then noitem = noitem + 1 else local entry = { ref = ref, nm = row.nm or "?", t = tostring(row.t), ar = row.ar or "?" } local id = resolve_ref(ref, idx) if not id then missing[#missing+1] = entry else byItem[id] = byItem[id] or {}; table.insert(byItem[id], entry) end end end db:close() return { byItem = byItem, missing = missing, total = total, noitem = noitem } end
-- Stamp each catalogued portal with the room it lands in, read from the mapper's -- saved portal exits (exits.touid on a '*'/'**' portal exit IS the room vnum). -- One saved destination -> that room number. A plain chaos portal saved to many -- rooms keeps a count instead, rather than a misleading single room. function pd_stamp_rooms(quiet) local x = cross_reference() if not x then return nil end local single, multi = 0, 0 for id, lst in pairs(x.byItem) do local e = catalog[id] if e then local seen, n, first = {}, 0, nil for _, ent in ipairs(lst) do local uid = ent.t if uid and uid ~= "" and uid ~= "nil" and not seen[uid] then seen[uid] = true n = n + 1 if not first then first = ent end end end if n == 1 then e.room, e.roomname = first.t, first.nm single = single + 1 else e.room, e.roomname = nil, nil if n > 1 then multi = multi + 1 end end e.rooms_n = n end end pd_save() if not quiet then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Landing rooms updated from the mapper: "..C.num..single ..C.hdr.." portal(s) with one destination, "..C.num..multi..C.hdr.." with several.") end return single end
function pd_rooms() pd_stamp_rooms(false) end
-- Catalogued portals still named "a golden chaos portal" and not flagged -- restrung: id'd before a restring, so the record may hold the stock name. -- Exact ref matches only (refs index or the id number itself): the keyword -- prefix fallback in resolve_ref could land on any golden. skip = ids -- already rechecked this scan. local function stale_golden_refs(skip) local path = get_db_path() if not path then return {} end local ok_sql, sqlite3 = pcall(require, "sqlite3") if not ok_sql then return {} end local db = sqlite3.open(path) if not db then return {} end local idx = build_ref_index() local list, seen = {}, {} for row in db:nrows("SELECT dir FROM exits WHERE fromuid IN ('*','**')") do local ref, container = extract_ref(row.dir) local bag = (pd_bag ~= "" and pd_bag) or container if ref and bag then local r = ref:lower() local id = idx[r] or (catalog[r] and r) local e = id and catalog[id] if e and not seen[id] and not (skip and skip[id]) and not e.restrung and (e.name or ""):lower() == "a golden chaos portal" then seen[id] = true list[#list+1] = { ref = ref, container = bag, recheck = id } end end end db:close() return list end
local function load_portal_refs(only_missing) local path, why = get_db_path() if not path then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] "..esc(why or "no mapper db")..".") return {} end local ok_sql, sqlite3 = pcall(require, "sqlite3") if not ok_sql then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] sqlite3 library unavailable.") return {} end local db = sqlite3.open(path) if not db then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] could not open the mapper database.") return {} end local check = only_missing and make_cataloged_checker() or nil local list, seen = {}, {} for row in db:nrows("SELECT dir FROM exits WHERE fromuid IN ('*','**')") do local ref, container = extract_ref(row.dir) local bag = (pd_bag ~= "" and pd_bag) or container if ref and bag and not seen[ref] then seen[ref] = true if (not check) or (not check(ref)) then list[#list+1] = { ref = ref, container = bag } end end end db:close() return list end
function pd_scan_finish_pass() local was_missing = (scan_mode == "missing") if scan_mode == "missing" then local remaining = load_portal_refs(true) if #remaining > 0 and #remaining < scan_pass_start then scan_pass_start = #remaining scan_queue = remaining scan_active = true echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Pass done — "..C.num..#remaining..C.hdr.." still missing, retrying...") pd_scan_step() return end scan_mode = nil echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Scan complete. "..C.num..#remaining..C.hdr.." still missing" ..((#remaining > 0) and (C.hdr.." (no progress last pass — "..C.ok.."portaldex missing"..C.hdr.." to inspect)") or "")..".") else echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Scan complete.") end pd_stamp_rooms(true) pd_summary() if was_missing then local checked, renamed = 0, 0 for id in pairs(scan_rechecked) do checked = checked + 1 local e = catalog[id] if e and (e.name or ""):lower() ~= "a golden chaos portal" then renamed = renamed + 1 end end if checked > 0 then echo(C.hdr.."[PortalDex] Re-checked "..C.num..checked..C.hdr.." golden chaos portals; " ..C.num..renamed..C.hdr.." had been restrung and now carry their new name.") end end end
function pd_scan_step() if not scan_active then return end local item = table.remove(scan_queue, 1) if not item then scan_active = false; pd_scan_finish_pass(); return end pd_scan_current_ref = (item.ref or ""):lower() if item.recheck then scan_rechecked[item.recheck] = true end Send("take " .. item.ref .. -- ===== "is this room worth a portal?" ================================== -- Answers, from your OWN data: if you put a portal in this room, how much -- walking would it save you across the mobs you actually kill, and how does -- that compare with the portals you already carry? -- -- Kill weights come from Search_and_Destroy's SnDdb.db when it is present -- (every mob row there carries a kill_count). Without SnD we weight every -- mapped room equally, which still answers "how much walking would a portal -- here save" -- just spread over the whole map instead of over your targets. -- -- Everything is measured against the portals YOU have and the mobs YOU kill, -- so there are no baked-in numbers: the "good portal" bar is the median value -- of your own portals.
local PW = { built = false }
local function pw_snd_path() for _, p in ipairs{ GetInfo(66) .. "SnDdb.db", GetInfo(66) .. "/SnDdb.db" } do local f = io.open(p, "rb") if f then f:close(); return p end end return nil end
local function pw_comma(n) local s = tostring(math.floor(tonumber(n) or 0)) local out = s:reverse():gsub("(%d%d%d)", "%1,"):reverse() return (out:gsub("^,", "")) end
-- Build the once-per-session model: nearest and second-nearest portal for every -- mapped room, plus how much walking each portal you own is uniquely saving. local function pw_build(dbpath) local ok_sql, sqlite3 = pcall(require, "sqlite3") if not ok_sql then return nil, "sqlite3 library unavailable" end local db = sqlite3.open(dbpath) if not db then return nil, "could not open the mapper database" end
local fadj, area_of = {}, {} for row in db:nrows("SELECT uid, area FROM rooms") do area_of[tostring(row.uid)] = row.area or "?" end -- rooms a portal cannot land in. Only the flagged ones are stored, which is -- a handful of rooms per area rather than a second copy of the whole map. local flags = {} for row in db:nrows("SELECT uid, norecall, noportal FROM rooms WHERE norecall=1 OR noportal=1") do flags[tostring(row.uid)] = { nr = (tonumber(row.norecall) or 0) == 1, np = (tonumber(row.noportal) or 0) == 1 } end for row in db:nrows("SELECT fromuid AS f, touid AS t FROM exits WHERE fromuid NOT IN ('*','**')") do local f = tostring(row.f) local b = fadj[f]; if not b then b = {}; fadj[f] = b end b[#b+1] = tostring(row.t) end
-- one label per distinct portal command, so two portals landing in one room -- stay distinct and a chained route counts once local seeds, seen = {}, {} for row in db:nrows("SELECT touid AS t, dir AS d FROM exits WHERE fromuid IN ('*','**')") do local cmd = tostring(row.d) seen[cmd] = true seeds[#seeds+1] = { uid = tostring(row.t), lab = cmd } end db:close() if next(seen) == nil then return nil, "no portals saved in the mapper yet" end
-- Nearest AND second-nearest DISTINCT portal, from every landing at once. -- The second pass is what lets us price the portals already carried: what a -- portal uniquely saves is the weight it is nearest to times (d2 - d1). -- Unit edges, so a plain FIFO queue keeps distances in order; no heap. local d1, l1, d2 = {}, {}, {} local q, head = {}, 1 for _, s in ipairs(seeds) do local u = s.uid if d1[u] == nil then d1[u] = 0; l1[u] = s.lab; q[#q+1] = { u, s.lab, 0 } elseif d2[u] == nil and l1[u] ~= s.lab then d2[u] = 0; q[#q+1] = { u, s.lab, 0 } end end while head <= #q do local it = q[head]; head = head + 1 local u, lab, d = it[1], it[2], it[3] local nb = fadj[u] if nb then for i = 1, #nb do local v, nd = nb[i], d + 1 if d1[v] == nil then d1[v] = nd; l1[v] = lab; q[#q+1] = { v, lab, nd } elseif d2[v] == nil and l1[v] ~= lab then d2[v] = nd; q[#q+1] = { v, lab, nd } end end end end
-- weights: kills per room if SnD is installed, otherwise every room counts 1 local kills, weighted = {}, false local sp = pw_snd_path() if sp then local sdb = sqlite3.open(sp) if sdb then local okq = pcall(function() for row in sdb:nrows("SELECT roomid AS r, SUM(kill_count) AS k FROM mobs WHERE kill_count>0 GROUP BY roomid") do kills[tostring(row.r)] = tonumber(row.k) or 0 weighted = true end end) if not okq then kills, weighted = {}, false end sdb:close() end end if not weighted then kills = {} for u in pairs(d1) do kills[u] = 1 end end
-- Everything below is PER AREA: a portal competes with the other portals -- that cover the same area, not with the whole collection. local kills_by_area = {} -- area -> { room = weight } local total_by_area = {} -- area -> steps currently walked there local weight_by_area = {} -- area -> total kill weight there local worst_by_area = {} -- area -> longest walk to any killed room there for r, k in pairs(kills) do local a = d1[r] if a then local ar = area_of[r] or "?" local kb = kills_by_area[ar]; if not kb then kb = {}; kills_by_area[ar] = kb end kb[r] = k total_by_area[ar] = (total_by_area[ar] or 0) + k * a weight_by_area[ar] = (weight_by_area[ar] or 0) + k if a > (worst_by_area[ar] or -1) then worst_by_area[ar] = a end end end
-- What each portal you already carry uniquely saves, map wide. This is the -- same figure that decides whether a portal is worth its item slot, so it is -- the honest yardstick for a candidate: a room that would land in the bottom -- quarter of this list is a room you would be selling again later. local marg = {} for r, k in pairs(kills) do local a = d1[r] if a then local b = d2[r] or (a + 30) -- nothing else reaches it: assume a long detour marg[l1[r]] = (marg[l1[r]] or 0) + k * (b - a) end end local ranked, nport = {}, 0 for cmd in pairs(seen) do nport = nport + 1 ranked[#ranked+1] = marg[cmd] or 0 end table.sort(ranked) local floor_val = (nport > 0) and ranked[math.ceil(nport / 4)] or 0 local mid_val = (nport > 0) and ranked[math.ceil(nport / 2)] or 0
return { built = true, fadj = fadj, d1 = d1, kills = kills, area_of = area_of, flags = flags, kills_by_area = kills_by_area, total_by_area = total_by_area, weight_by_area = weight_by_area, worst_by_area = worst_by_area, floor_val = floor_val, mid_val = mid_val, nport = nport, weighted = weighted } end
local function pw_model(dbpath) if PW.built then return PW end local t0 = os.clock() local m, why = pw_build(dbpath) if not m then return nil, why end PW = m if pv_debug then pv_echo(C.hdr .. "[PortalValue] worth model built in " .. C.num .. string.format("%.2f", os.clock() - t0) .. C.hdr .. "s over " .. C.num .. m.nport .. C.hdr .. " portals.") end return PW end
-- How much walking a portal landing in room T would save inside T's OWN area, -- and where that puts it among the portals already covering that area. local function pw_evaluate(T, area, dbpath) local m, why = pw_model(dbpath) if not m then return nil, why end area = area or m.area_of[T] or "?"
local targets = m.kills_by_area[area] if not targets then local f = m.flags[T] or {} return { area = area, save = 0, pct = 0, weighted = m.weighted, verdict = "nodata", noportal = f.np, norecall = f.nr } end
local dT, q, head = { [T] = 0 }, { T }, 1 while head <= #q do local u = q[head]; head = head + 1 local nb = m.fadj[u] if nb then for i = 1, #nb do local v = nb[i] if dT[v] == nil then dT[v] = dT[u] + 1; q[#q+1] = v end end end end
-- Average is not enough on its own: a room can rack up a big total and still -- leave the far end of the area untouched. Track the worst remaining walk too, -- which is what separates a junction serving the whole area from a spot that -- only shortens the half you were already close to. local save, new_sum, new_worst = 0, 0, 0 for r, k in pairs(targets) do local a, b = m.d1[r], dT[r] local best = a if a and b and b < a then save = save + k * (a - b); best = b end if best then new_sum = new_sum + k * best if best > new_worst then new_worst = best end end end
local tot = m.total_by_area[area] or 0 local wsum = m.weight_by_area[area] or 0 local worst = m.worst_by_area[area] or 0 local pct = (tot > 0) and (100 * save / tot) or 0 local tailpct = (worst > 0) and (100 * (worst - new_worst) / worst) or 0 local cur_avg = (wsum > 0) and (tot / wsum) or 0 local new_avg = (wsum > 0) and (new_sum / wsum) or 0 -- weighted toward the average, because that is most of the walking, but with -- enough of the tail to prefer a junction that also reaches the far rooms local score = 0.75 * pct + 0.25 * tailpct
-- Two gates, because neither alone is honest. The percentage is how much of -- your walking IN THIS AREA a portal here would cut, which is the thing you -- actually feel. The pool median stops a well covered area from rewarding -- yet another portal -- but only once the pool is big enough for a median to -- mean anything; with two portals, "beats the median" just means "beats the -- worse of the two", which would wave almost anything through. -- A percentage alone is scale blind: a small area can hand you "29% less -- walking" for a few hundred steps, which is exactly the profile of a portal -- you would later sell. So the absolute saving has to clear the bottom -- quarter of what your existing portals are worth before the share matters, -- and "good" has to clear the median as well. local verdict if save <= 0 then verdict = "none" elseif save < m.floor_val then verdict = "skip" elseif score >= 15 and save >= m.mid_val then verdict = "good" elseif score >= 5 then verdict = "ok" else verdict = "skip" end
local f = m.flags[T] or {} return { area = area, save = save, pct = pct, score = score, tailpct = tailpct, floor_val = m.floor_val, cur_avg = cur_avg, new_avg = new_avg, cur_worst = worst, new_worst = new_worst, weighted = m.weighted, verdict = verdict, noportal = f.np, norecall = f.nr } end
function pv_worth_lines(r) if r.w_msg then pv_echo(C.hdr .. "Worth it : " .. C.bad .. esc(r.w_msg)) return end if not r.w_verdict then return end if r.w_verdict == "nodata" then pv_echo(C.hdr .. "Worth it : " .. C.val .. "no kills recorded in " .. C.val .. esc(r.w_area or "?") .. C.hdr .. " yet, so there is nothing to weigh a portal against." .. (r.w_noportal and (C.bad .. "[PortalValue] Landing room " .. C.num .. esc(T) .. C.hdr .. " isn't mapped yet, so I can't compute a path.") return end
local have_portal_here = false for _ in db:nrows(string.format( "SELECT 1 AS x FROM exits WHERE fromuid IN ('*','**') AND touid=%s LIMIT 1", q(T))) do have_portal_here = true end
local radj = {} for row in db:nrows("SELECT fromuid AS f, touid AS t, dir AS d FROM exits WHERE fromuid NOT IN ('*','**')") do local t = tostring(row.t) local bucket = radj[t] if not bucket then bucket = {}; radj[t] = bucket end bucket[#bucket+1] = { from = tostring(row.f), dir = row.d } end
local portals = {} for row in db:nrows([[ SELECT e.touid AS t, e.dir AS d, e.level AS lv, r.name AS nm, r.area AS ar FROM exits e JOIN rooms r ON r.uid = e.touid WHERE e.fromuid IN ('*','**') ]]) do portals[#portals+1] = { uid = tostring(row.t), cmd = row.d, level = row.lv, name = row.nm, area = row.ar } end

local dist = { [T] = 0 } local fwd = {} local queue, head = { T }, 1 while head <= #queue do local cur = queue[head]; head = head + 1 local d0 = dist[cur] local preds = radj[cur] if preds then for _, pe in ipairs(preds) do local p = pe.from if dist[p] == nil then dist[p] = d0 + 1 fwd[p] = { dir = pe.dir, nxt = cur } queue[#queue+1] = p end end end end

local function rgb_to_xterm (n) if not n then return 7 end local r = n % 256 local g = math.floor(n / 256) % 256 local b = math.floor(n / 65536) % 256 if r == g and g == b then if r < 8 then return 16 end if r > 238 then return 231 end return math.floor((r - 8) / 10) + 232 end local function to6 (v) if v < 48 then return 0 elseif v < 115 then return 1 elseif v < 155 then return 2 elseif v < 195 then return 3 elseif v < 235 then return 4 else return 5 end end return 16 + 36 * to6(r) + 6 * to6(g) + to6(b) end

-- Portals recorded with a bag or a restore step that is no longer current. -- Changing bags, swapping your dual weapon, or flipping wish mode makes -- every previously recorded exit stale, because the command string stored -- in the mapper still names the old items. local function staleList () local stale = {} local restore = restoreToken () local bag = bagToken () for serial, m in pairs (gMapped) do if m.bag and m.restore and (m.bag ~= bag or m.restore ~= restore) then table.insert (stale, serial) end end table.sort (stale) return stale end
-- Is the Aardwolf mapper there to take our exits? local function mapperReady () if not IsPluginInstalled (MAPPER_ID) then return false, "the Aardwolf mapper plugin is not installed." end if GetPluginInfo (MAPPER_ID, 17) == false then return false, "the Aardwolf mapper plugin is disabled." end return true end
-- Read-only look at the mapper's own database. local function openMapperDb () local name = GetPluginVariable (MAPPER_ID, "db_name") if not name or name == "" then return nil end local ok, db = pcall (sqlite3.open, GetInfo (66) .. name .. ".db") if not ok or not db then return nil end pcall (function () db:busy_timeout (200) end) return db end
-- Is this portal's exit in the mapper, the way 'mapper portals' would list -- it (exit from anywhere, destination room known)? room is optional. -- true / false, or nil if the database could not be queried. -- -- v1.5: matches the serial anywhere in the stored command, as a whole -- number, because a custom command need not say "wear <n>;enter". LIKE -- narrows it down, then a frontier pattern stops 3828209 matching 13828209. local function exitInMapper (db, serial, room) serial = tostring (serial or "") if not string.match (serial, "^%d+$") then return nil end if room and not string.match (tostring (room), "^%-?%d+$") then return nil end local q = "SELECT exits.dir AS dir FROM exits LEFT OUTER JOIN rooms ON rooms.uid = exits.touid " .. "WHERE exits.fromuid IN ('*','**') AND rooms.area IS NOT NULL " .. "AND exits.dir LIKE '%" .. serial .. "%' " .. (room and ("AND CAST(exits.touid AS TEXT) = '" .. room .. "' ") or "") local ok, found = pcall (function () for row in db:nrows (q) do if string.find (row.dir or "", "%f[%d]" .. serial .. "%f[%D]") then return true end end return false end) if not ok then return nil end return found end
-- What is still missing before a run can start? local function missingConfig () local missing = {} if not gCfg.bag then table.insert (missing, "portalmapper bag <id> (or endbag - same thing)") end local mode = modeName () if mode == "custom" then -- only needed if the custom command actually uses those words if hasWord (gCfg.custom, "wearportal") and not gCfg.wearportal then table.insert (missing, "portalmapper wearportal <id> (your custom command uses wearportal)") end if hasWord (gCfg.custom, "dualweapon") and not gCfg.dualweapon then table.insert (missing, "portalmapper dualweapon <id> (your custom command uses dualweapon)") end if gCfg.startbag then local before, after = templateBagSides (gCfg.custom) if not (before and after) then table.insert (missing, "a start bag needs the word 'bag' in your custom command, " .. "before AND after the enter step - or: portalmapper startbag off") end end elseif mode == "wish" then if not gCfg.wearportal then table.insert (missing, "portalmapper wearportal <id>") end else if not gCfg.dualweapon then table.insert (missing, "portalmapper dualweapon <id>") end end return missing end
-- The bag a run looks in: the start bag if there is one, else the bag. local function scanBag () return gCfg.startbag or gCfg.bag end
-- For the live run only: point the bag word at the START bag. Used on the -- way in (take it out of the start bag) and when a portal fails (put it -- back there). The recorded command never sees this - it always says -- portalbag, which is the end bag, where the portal lives once mapped. local function toStartBag (step) if not gCfg.startbag then return step end return replaceWord (step, "portalbag", gCfg.startbag) end
-- ===================================================================== -- Data file -- -- Settings and the mapped list live together in one plain text file next -- to the plugin. GetPluginInfo(id, 6) is the .xml FILE path, not the -- folder - gluing a name straight on silently produces -- "PortalMapper.xml_data.txt", so trim back to the last separator. -- ===================================================================== local function dataPath () local pluginFile = GetPluginInfo (GetPluginID (), 6) or "" local pluginDir = string.match (pluginFile, "^(.*[\\/])") or "" return pluginDir .. "PortalMapper_data.txt" end
local function saveData () local path = dataPath () local f, err = io.open (path, "w") if not f then echoWarn ("could not write " .. path .. ": " .. tostring (err)) return false end
f:write ("# PortalMapper data - settings and mapped portals.\n") f:write ("# set <name> <value>\n") f:write ("# map <serial>|<room>|<level>|<bag>|<restore step>|<name>\n") f:write ("# The bag and restore step are the ones in force WHEN IT WAS RECORDED,\n") f:write ("# which is how 'portalmapper rewrite' knows what to change.\n") if gCfg.bag then f:write ("set bag " .. gCfg.bag .. "\n") end if gCfg.dualweapon then f:write ("set dualweapon " .. gCfg.dualweapon .. "\n") end if gCfg.wearportal then f:write ("set wearportal " .. gCfg.wearportal .. "\n") end f:write ("set wish " .. (gCfg.wish and "1" or "0") .. "\n") if gCfg.startbag then f:write ("set startbag " .. gCfg.startbag .. "\n") end if gCfg.custom then f:write ("set custom " .. gCfg.custom .. "\n") end f:write ("set customon " .. (gCfg.customOn and "1" or "0") .. "\n")
local serials = {} for s in pairs (gMapped) do table.insert (serials, s) end table.sort (serials) for _, s in ipairs (serials) do local m = gMapped [s] f:write (string.format ("map %s|%s|%s|%s|%s|%s\n", s, m.room, m.level, m.bag or "", m.restore or "", m.name or "")) end
f:close () if cfgRedraw then cfgRedraw () end return true end
local function loadData () gCfg.bag, gCfg.dualweapon, gCfg.wearportal = nil, nil, nil gCfg.wish = false gCfg.custom, gCfg.customOn, gCfg.startbag = nil, false, nil gMapped = {}
local f = io.open (dataPath (), "r") if not f then return end
for raw in f:lines () do local line = trim (raw) if line ~= "" and string.sub (line, 1, 1) ~= "#" then local key, value = string.match (line, "^set%s+(%S+)%s+(.+)$") if key then if key == "wish" then gCfg.wish = (value == "1") elseif key == "customon" then gCfg.customOn = (value == "1") elseif key == "bag" or key == "dualweapon" or key == "wearportal" or key == "startbag" or key == "custom" then gCfg [key] = value end else -- current format: map serial|room|level|bag|restore|name local serial, room, level, bag, restore, name = string.match (line, "^map%s+([^|]+)|([^|]*)|([^|]*)|([^|]*)|([^|]*)|(.*)$")
if not serial then -- v1.0 format: map serial room level name. No bag or restore was -- stored, so those stay nil and "rewrite" leaves the record alone -- rather than guessing what it was recorded with. serial, room, level, name = string.match (line, "^map%s+(%d+)%s+(%-?%d+)%s+(%d+)%s*(.*)$") bag, restore = nil, nil end
if serial then gMapped [trim (serial)] = { room = room, level = level, bag = (bag ~= "" and bag) or nil, restore = (restore ~= "" and restore) or nil, name = name, } end end end end
f:close () end
-- ===================================================================== -- invdata scan of the bag -- ===================================================================== local function stopScanTriggers () EnableTrigger ("pm_inv_header", false) EnableTriggerGroup ("pm_inv_body", false) end
local function beginScan (want) gScan = { want = want, items = {}, ticks = 0, bag = scanBag () } gStep = "scanning" EnableTrigger ("pm_inv_header", true) EnableTimer ("pm_tick", true) ResetTimer ("pm_tick") SendNoEcho ("invdata " .. gScan.bag) end
function pmInvHeader (name, line, wildcards) -- Only ours: another plugin's inventory scan answers with a different -- container id, or with the bare "{invdata}" header this does not match. if not gScan then EnableTrigger ("pm_inv_header", false) return end if wildcards [1] ~= gScan.bag then return end
EnableTrigger ("pm_inv_header", false) EnableTriggerGroup ("pm_inv_body", true) end
function pmInvItem (name, line, wildcards) if not gScan then return end table.insert (gScan.items, { serial = wildcards [1], flags = wildcards [2], name = stripColours (wildcards [3]), level = wildcards [4], itype = tonumber (wildcards [5]) or 0, }) end
-- forward declarations local nextPortal, finishRun, startRun
function pmInvFooter () stopScanTriggers () if not gScan then return end
local scan = gScan gScan = nil gStep = "idle" EnableTimer ("pm_tick", false)
-- Never trust our own list over the mapper's: forget anything we think -- is mapped that the mapper does not actually have. do local db = openMapperDb () if db then local dropped = 0 for _, item in ipairs (scan.items) do if item.itype == ITEM_TYPE_PORTAL and gMapped [item.serial] and exitInMapper (db, item.serial) == false then gMapped [item.serial] = nil dropped = dropped + 1 end end pcall (function () db:close () end) if dropped > 0 then saveData () echoWarn (dropped .. " portal(s) were recorded earlier but are NOT in " .. "'mapper portals' - they will be mapped again.") end end end
local portals, already, other = {}, 0, 0 local alreadyList = {} for _, item in ipairs (scan.items) do if item.itype ~= ITEM_TYPE_PORTAL then other = other + 1 elseif gMapped [item.serial] then already = already + 1 table.insert (alreadyList, item) else table.insert (portals, item) end end
local fromStart = gCfg.startbag and scan.bag == gCfg.startbag and gCfg.startbag ~= gCfg.bag
if scan.want == "list" then echoHi (fromStart and "start bag " or "bag ", tostring (scan.bag), " holds " .. #scan.items .. " item(s):") echoHi (" portals not yet mapped : ", tostring (#portals), "") echoHi (" portals already mapped : ", tostring (already), "") echoHi (" not portals (ignored) : ", tostring (other), "") for _, p in ipairs (portals) do ColourNote (CLR_HI, "", string.format (" %-12s", p.serial), CLR_MSG, "", "L" .. p.level .. " " .. p.name) end return end
-- want == "run"
-- Start bag: anything in it that is ALREADY mapped just moves across to -- the end bag - no need to walk it again. if fromStart and #alreadyList > 0 then for _, item in ipairs (alreadyList) do SendNoEcho ("get " .. item.serial .. " " .. gCfg.startbag) SendNoEcho ("put " .. item.serial .. " " .. gCfg.bag) end echoHi ("moved ", tostring (#alreadyList), " already-mapped portal(s) from the start bag to the end bag.") end
if #portals == 0 then if fromStart then echoHi ("no unmapped portals in start bag ", tostring (scan.bag), ".") elseif already > 0 then echoHi ("nothing new in the bag - all ", tostring (already), " portal(s) in there are already mapped.") else echoHi ("no unmapped portals found in bag ", tostring (scan.bag), ".") end return end
gRun = { queue = portals, index = 0, stopping = false, done = 0, skipped = 0 } echoHi ("mapping ", tostring (#portals), " portal(s)" .. ((already > 0 and not fromStart) and (", skipping " .. already .. " already known") or "") .. (fromStart and (" from the start bag; each goes to the end bag once mapped") or "") .. ". 'portalmapper stop' halts after the current one.") nextPortal () end
-- ===================================================================== -- The run -- ===================================================================== -- Everything after the enter step: gear back on, portal back in the bag. -- -- Every step is Execute()d, not sent: the alias WORDS (dualweapon, -- portalbag, a custom command's own aliases) then go through exactly the -- path the mapper will use later, so a broken alias shows up here and not -- weeks from now. -- -- backToStart: the portal was NOT mapped, so with a start bag it goes back -- there instead of into the end bag. local function sendRestore (backToStart) for _, step in ipairs (gCurrent.post or {}) do Execute (backToStart and toStartBag (step) or step) end end
function finishRun (why) gStep = "idle" gCurrent = nil EnableTimer ("pm_tick", false)
local run = gRun gRun = nil if not run then return end
echoHi (why .. " - mapped ", tostring (run.done), " portal(s)" .. (run.skipped > 0 and (", skipped " .. run.skipped) or "") .. ". Total known: " .. countMapped () .. ".") if (run.unverified or 0) > 0 then echoWarn (run.unverified .. " portal(s) were confirmed only by the mapper's" .. " message, not checked in its database - see 'mapper portals'.") end end
-- Walk the next portal in the queue. function nextPortal () if not gRun then return end
if gRun.stopping then finishRun ("Stopped") return end
gRun.index = gRun.index + 1 if gRun.index > #gRun.queue then finishRun ("Finished") return end
gCurrent = gRun.queue [gRun.index] gFromRoom = gRoomNum gTicks = 0 gSawSame = false gStep = "entering"
dbg ("portal " .. gCurrent.serial .. " from room " .. tostring (gFromRoom))
-- Split the recorded command at its enter step: the first half is run -- now, the second half once we have arrived (sendRestore). local steps, enterAt = stepsFor (gCurrent.serial, bagToken (), restoreToken ()) gCurrent.pre, gCurrent.post = {}, {} for i, step in ipairs (steps) do if i <= enterAt then table.insert (gCurrent.pre, step) else table.insert (gCurrent.post, step) end end
-- Execute, not Send: these go through the same aliases the mapper will -- use later, so the live run is a real test of the stored command. The -- one live-only difference: with a start bag, the portal comes out of -- the start bag rather than the end bag the recorded command names. for _, step in ipairs (gCurrent.pre) do Execute (toStartBag (step)) end
EnableTimer ("pm_tick", true) ResetTimer ("pm_tick") end
-- The mapper's answer was good (or at least not bad). Keep the record. local function recordDone (unverified) local rec = gRec gRec = nil if not rec then return end local portal = rec.portal
gMapped [portal.serial] = { room = rec.room, level = portal.level, bag = bagToken (), restore = restoreToken (), name = portal.name, } saveData ()
gStep = "idle" if not gRun then return end
gRun.done = gRun.done + 1 if unverified then gRun.unverified = (gRun.unverified or 0) + 1 end
ColourNote (CLR_TAG, "", "[", CLR_NAME, "", TAG, CLR_TAG, "", "] ", CLR_MSG, "", string.format ("%d/%d ", gRun.index, #gRun.queue), CLR_HI, "", portal.serial, CLR_MSG, "", " L" .. portal.level .. " " .. portal.name .. " -> room ", CLR_HI, "", rec.room, CLR_WARN, "", unverified and " (confirmed by mapper message only)" or "")
nextPortal () end
-- The mapper refused every attempt. Nothing was stored - say so and halt. local function recordFailed () local rec = gRec gRec = nil gStep = "idle" if not rec then return end
echoWarn ("the mapper would not store portal " .. rec.portal.serial .. " (" .. rec.portal.name .. ") - it was NOT recorded.")
-- It already went into the end bag on arrival. Not mapped, so with a -- start bag it belongs back there. if gCfg.startbag and gCfg.startbag ~= gCfg.bag then SendNoEcho ("get " .. rec.portal.serial .. " " .. gCfg.bag) SendNoEcho ("put " .. rec.portal.serial .. " " .. gCfg.startbag) echo ("put it back in the start bag.") end echo ("mapper said: " .. tostring (gRecFail or "(nothing)")) echo ("If it says the room is unknown, the mapper has no data for room " .. rec.room .. ": check the mapper plugin is enabled, 'look' there, " .. "then move somewhere you can portal from and: portalmapper resume")
local run = gRun gRun = nil gCurrent = nil if run then echoHi ("mapped ", tostring (run.done), " portal(s) this run.") end end
local function attemptRecord () if not gRec then return end gRecFail, gRecOk = nil, false gRecGen = gRecGen + 1
local cmd = portalCommand (gRec.portal.serial)
-- No "quiet": the mapper's "Storing ... as a portal" line is how we know -- it worked, and its FAILED line is how we know it did not. Execute ("mapper fullportal {" .. cmd .. "} {" .. gRec.room .. "} " .. gRec.portal.level)
DoAfterSpecial (REC_DELAY, "pmRecCheck (" .. gRecGen .. ")", 12) end
-- Called REC_DELAY seconds after each fullportal attempt. function pmRecCheck (gen) if not gRec or gen ~= gRecGen then return end
local inDb = nil local db = openMapperDb () if db then inDb = exitInMapper (db, gRec.portal.serial, gRec.room) pcall (function () db:close () end) end
if inDb == true then recordDone (false) return end
if inDb == nil and not gRecFail then -- cannot read the database: trust the mapper's own confirmation line, -- and nothing less. if gRecOk then recordDone (true) return end gRecFail = "(no confirmation from the mapper, and its database could not be read)" elseif not gRecFail then gRecFail = "(the exit is not in the mapper's portal list)" end
gRec.tries = gRec.tries + 1 if gRec.tries < REC_RETRIES then dbg ("not stored (" .. gRecFail .. "), retry " .. gRec.tries) attemptRecord () else recordFailed () end end
-- The mapper reports through print(), which is a Note. Notes cannot be -- trigger matched but they do pass through here. function OnPluginScreendraw (t, log, line) if not gRec or not line then return end if string.find (line, "PORTAL", 1, true) and string.find (line, "FAILED", 1, true) then gRecFail = line elseif string.find (line, "as a portal to room", 1, true) then gRecOk = true end end
-- We went somewhere. Record it (when we can) and carry on. local function arrived (roomNum) local portal = gCurrent gStep = "idle" EnableTimer ("pm_tick", false)
if roomNum == "-1" then -- A real move, but the mud will not give this room a number, so the -- mapper cannot hold an exit to it. Not a failure - just skip it. gRun.skipped = gRun.skipped + 1 echoWarn ("portal " .. portal.serial .. " leads somewhere unmappable " .. "(room -1) - not recorded, carrying on.") sendRestore (true) nextPortal () return end
-- Gear back on while we wait for the mapper; the next portal only starts -- once the mapper has answered for this one. gStep = "recording" gRec = { portal = portal, room = roomNum, tries = 0 } sendRestore () attemptRecord () end
-- "enter" did nothing. Almost always a noportal room. local function enterFailed () local portal = gCurrent gStep = "idle" EnableTimer ("pm_tick", false)
echoWarn ("Make sure you can enter portal here before typing portalmapper resume") echoHi ("stopped on portal ", portal.serial, " (" .. portal.name .. ") - it was NOT recorded.")
-- Honest reporting of the one case this cannot tell apart from a failure: -- a portal whose destination is the room you are already standing in. if gSawSame then echo ("(the mud re-sent this same room while waiting - if that portal " .. "leads right back here, it looks identical to a failure)") end
sendRestore (true)
local run = gRun gRun = nil gCurrent = nil if run then echoHi ("mapped ", tostring (run.done), " portal(s) this run." .. " Move somewhere you can portal from, then: portalmapper resume") end end
-- ===================================================================== -- One second watchdog - the only thing it does is give up -- ===================================================================== function pmTick () if gStep == "entering" then gTicks = gTicks + 1 if gTicks >= ENTER_TIMEOUT then enterFailed () end return end
if gStep == "scanning" and gScan then gScan.ticks = gScan.ticks + 1 if gScan.ticks >= SCAN_TIMEOUT then local want = gScan.want gScan = nil gStep = "idle" stopScanTriggers () EnableTimer ("pm_tick", false) echoWarn ("no invdata reply for bag " .. tostring (gScan and gScan.bag or scanBag ()) .. " - is that the right bag id?") if want == "run" then echoHi ("check it with ", "portalmapper scan", "") end end return end
EnableTimer ("pm_tick", false) end
-- ===================================================================== -- GMCP room.info (telnet option 201) -- ===================================================================== function OnPluginTelnetSubnegotiation (theType, data) if theType ~= 201 then return end
local message = string.match (data, "^([%w%.%-_]+)") if not message then return end if string.lower (message) ~= "room.info" then return end
local num = string.match (data, '"num"%s*:%s*(%-?%d+)') if not num then return end
gRoomNum = num
if gStep == "entering" and num ~= gFromRoom then arrived (num) elseif gStep == "entering" then gSawSame = true dbg ("room.info still room " .. num .. ", waiting") end end
-- Read the current room without waiting for a move. local function syncRoom () if gHaveGmcpHelper then local ok, num = pcall (gmcp, "room.info.num") if ok and num ~= nil then gRoomNum = tostring (num) return true end pcall (Send_GMCP_Packet, "request room") end return false end
-- ===================================================================== -- Alias callbacks -- ===================================================================== function startRun () if gRun or gStep ~= "idle" then echo ("already running - 'portalmapper stop' to halt after this portal.") return end
local missing = missingConfig () if #missing > 0 then echoWarn ("not set up yet. Still needed:") for _, m in ipairs (missing) do ColourNote (CLR_HI, "", " " .. m) end echoHi ("full setup: ", "pmhelp", "") return end
if modeName () == "custom" then local problem = templateProblem (gCfg.custom) if problem then echoWarn ("your custom command will not work: " .. problem) echoHi ("set it again with ", "portalmapper custom <command>", "") return end end
local ready, why = mapperReady () if not ready then echoWarn (why .. " Nothing can be recorded without it.") return end
syncRoom () if not gRoomNum then echo ("I do not know what room you are in yet - type 'look' and try again.") return end if gRoomNum == "-1" then echoWarn ("this room has no room number, so nothing can be recorded from here.") echo ("move to a normal room and try again.") return end
beginScan ("run") end

function pmAliasList () local n = countMapped () if n == 0 then echo ("no portals mapped yet.") return end
echoHi ("", tostring (n), " portal(s) on record:") local serials = {} for s in pairs (gMapped) do table.insert (serials, s) end table.sort (serials) local db = openMapperDb () local missing = 0 for _, s in ipairs (serials) do local m = gMapped [s] local gone = db and exitInMapper (db, s) == false if gone then missing = missing + 1 end ColourNote (CLR_HI, "", string.format (" %-12s", s), CLR_MSG, "", string.format ("room %-8s L%-4s %s", m.room, m.level, m.name or ""), CLR_WARN, "", gone and " NOT IN MAPPER" or "") end if db then pcall (function () db:close () end) end if missing > 0 then echoWarn (missing .. " of those are not in 'mapper portals' - " .. "'portalmapper go' will map them again.") end echoHi ("re-map one with ", "portalmapper forget <serial>", "") end
function pmAliasForget (name, line, wildcards) local serial = wildcards [1] if not gMapped [serial] then echoHi ("not in the mapped list: ", serial, "") return end gMapped [serial] = nil saveData () echoHi ("forgotten ", serial, " - the next 'portalmapper go' will map it again.") echo ("(this does not remove the exit from the mapper - 'mapper portals' does that)") end
function pmAliasForgetAll () local n = countMapped () gMapped = {} saveData () echoHi ("cleared all ", tostring (n), " remembered portal(s).") echo ("(the mapper's own portal exits are untouched)") end
-- Say something if this change just orphaned previously recorded portals. local function warnIfStale () local stale = staleList () if #stale == 0 then return end echoWarn (#stale .. " portal(s) already in the mapper were recorded with a " .. "different command (older mode or custom command).") echoHi ("fix them all with ", "portalmapper rewrite", " - no re-walking, it just edits the stored commands.") end
local function setSerial (which, label, value) gCfg [which] = value saveData () echoHi (label .. " set to ", value, "") local missing = missingConfig () if #missing == 0 then echoHi ("setup complete - run it with ", "portalmapper go", "") end warnIfStale () end
-- Re-point every already-recorded portal exit at the current bag and the -- current restore step, without walking anything. -- -- "mapper change portal {old} {new}" does an in-place UPDATE of the exit's -- command, keeping its destination and level (aard_GMCP_mapper.xml, -- map_portal_edit). Both strings go through Execute, so both use the same -- computed separator as everything else. function pmAliasRewrite () if gRun or gStep ~= "idle" then echo ("busy right now - try again when the run has stopped.") return end
local missing = missingConfig () if #missing > 0 then echoWarn ("set the bag and the restore item first - see pmhelp.") return end
local stale = staleList () if #stale == 0 then local unknown = 0 for _, m in pairs (gMapped) do if not (m.bag and m.restore) then unknown = unknown + 1 end end if unknown > 0 then echoHi ("nothing to rewrite, but ", tostring (unknown), " old record(s) predate this feature and do not say which bag " .. "they used - those have to be re-walked if the bag changed.") echoHi ("to re-walk them: ", "portalmapper forget all", " then portalmapper go") else echo ("nothing to rewrite - every recorded portal already matches your " .. "current bag and restore step.") end return end
local restore = restoreToken () local bag = bagToken () for _, serial in ipairs (stale) do local m = gMapped [serial] local oldCmd = portalCommandFor (serial, m.bag, m.restore) local newCmd = portalCommandFor (serial, bag, restore)
Execute ("mapper change portal {" .. oldCmd .. "} {" .. newCmd .. "}")
m.bag = bag m.restore = restore end
saveData () echoHi ("rewrote ", tostring (#stale), " portal exit(s) to the current " .. modeName () .. " mode command.") echo ("the mapper prints one confirmation line per portal above.") end
-- "dualweapon" typed, or reached from a stored portal command. function pmAliasDoDual () if not gCfg.dualweapon then echoWarn ("no dual weapon set - portalmapper dualweapon <id>") return end SendNoEcho ("dual " .. gCfg.dualweapon) end
-- "wearportal" typed, or reached from a stored portal command. function pmAliasDoWear () if not gCfg.wearportal then echoWarn ("no wear-portal item set - portalmapper wearportal <id>") return end SendNoEcho ("wear " .. gCfg.wearportal) end
-- "get <serial> portalbag" / "put <serial> portalbag", from a stored -- portal command or typed by hand. local function bagOrComplain () if not gCfg.bag then echoWarn ("no portal bag set - portalmapper bag <id>") return nil end return gCfg.bag end
-- "<verb> <serial> portalbag" - get, take, put, whatever the command says. function pmAliasDoBag (name, line, wildcards) local bag = bagOrComplain () if bag then SendNoEcho (wildcards [1] .. " " .. wildcards [2] .. " " .. bag) end end

-- A custom command is typed with semicolons in it. Command stacking would -- split the line at the first one before any alias saw it, and the rest -- (wear port, ent port, ...) would go to the mud. This callback gets the -- WHOLE line first (MUSHclient sendvw.cpp: OnPluginCommandEntered runs -- before SendCommand), so take it here and return "\t", which tells the -- client to discard the line. function OnPluginCommandEntered (sText) local t = trim (sText or "") local rest = string.match (t, "^portalmapper%s+custom(.*)$") if rest and (rest == "" or string.match (rest, "^%s")) then pmCustomSet (rest) return "\t" end return sText end
